items.title: AI agents design an entirely new CPU architecture from scratch, startup claims
items.description: Architect Labs says its AI agents designed Frostbite, an interaction-net CPU with 4.59x the performance per watt of an in-order core.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Architect Labs, a Palo Alto startup, said in a research blog post that its AI systems discovered, designed, and verified Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set “built from the ground up.” Across 25 workloads, a four-tile Frostbite cluster delivered 4.59 times the performance per watt of a similarly sized “silicon-proven” dual-issue, in-order CPU core. Those numbers come from a simulated 7nm design that has not yet been made in silicon, and the company says it can’t name the comparison core for legal reasons.Conventional CPUs have hardware that “rediscovers, at runtime, which instructions actually depend on each other.” Multicore designs also need deep cache hierarchies and coherence protocols, which keep every core’s view of shared memory consistent, but scale poorly and cost area and power. Architect Labs’ alternative is what it calls “multithreading for free,” where the program itself exposes the parallel work, without threads, locks, or out-of-order hardware required for that discovery.Frostbite’s programs are compiled to interaction nets, a model of computation from 1990 in which a program is a graph of nodes and computation happens by rewriting pairs of connected nodes, and the chip is designed around this distinct paradigm. Pairs of nodes being rewritten never overlap, so they can run in any order, or all at once, and arrive at the same result. Every value is also used exactly once, so data can stay in small local memories instead of large shared caches.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: An example of the difference given by the team is a 5x5 chess-like board with five queens, placed so none can attack another. A typical program searches for solutions one board at a time. As an interaction net, the same search breaks into 3,183 small operations, and the longest chain that has to run in order is only 262 steps, so on average about 12 operations are ready to run at once at each step. Nothing about the program was rewritten to get there, as the parallel work was already intrinsic. (Image credit: Architect Labs)Each of the chip’s tiles, small identical processing units linked by an on-chip network, has its own small local memory. Four tiles, plus four L3 nodes, form the cluster that’s benchmarked against the conventional core for the performance claims, but the full layout has 16 tiles. The design reached 800 MHz in early synthesis but ended up at 500 MHz in the final layout. The cluster also averaged 8.77 times the comparison core’s performance per area, and the table below shows how its performance per watt varies by workload. You may like Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests Nuvacore reveals unconventional Core First CPU IP design strategy Bizarre AI chip demo uses butter to highlight how new chip runs 40 degrees cooler than the competition Swipe to scroll horizontally How Frostbite’s efficiency gains vary by workload Workloads Frostbite performance per watt vs. comparison core All 25 (geometric mean) 4.59x 10 used to tune the design 6.02x 15 held out until the final evaluation 3.83x Best: conv2d (held out) 23.12x Worst: recursive Fibonacci (held out) 1.15x It may come as some surprise that the AI which built Frostbite started with what the company calls “zero architectural priors,” though the team first picked the workloads it had to do well on, and this sort of blank slatism may have its advantages in avoiding bias. Instead, the agents read papers and benchmarks, built Python models, and then selected one concept for focus. The original 141-page PDF output, which contained a programming model, runtime, and high-level blocks, was deleted after the first register-transfer level (RTL) design was generated, because “many of the numbers and estimates were well off what was physically possible.”That PDF was only ever a starting point. Once the agents picked an architecture, they moved away from English — as it can’t get every detail right or catch every mistake, according to the team — and wrote the spec in the company’s own language, called ASL. ASL translates to Lean, a proof checker, so it can be machine-checked, which the company says stops a large class of bugs and cuts down on agents gaming their objectives. From this, the agents devised Arcmodel, a software model of the whole chip written in ASL, before any circuit design existed.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsSimulating the RTL is slow, so the agents tested ideas on the model instead, which ran about 200 times faster. At first, the model’s power estimates were off by up to almost 250%, but an automated loop adjusted it until it matched the circuit design within just 5%.From there, swarms of agents proposed changes in parallel, and each one was checked against the spec, tried in the fast model, built into the circuit design, and measured for power before being kept or dropped. This led to 58 ideas tried, with 37 kept. Separately, a behavior emerged that “was never specified by any human,” in what is known as work stealing: a tile with nothing to do can pull spare work from a neighbor or, in lieu of anything to do, go idle to save power. Swipe to scroll horizontally Where each chip’s energy goes Share of energy (one four-tile cluster, mean of 20 workloads, excluding clock distribution) Comparison core Frostbite Memory 57% 38% Fetching, decoding, and issuing instructions 27% 6% On-chip network and scheduler Not broken out 26% Clock distribution (share of total energy, left out of the rows above) 49% 41% This isn’t Architect Labs’ first design, as it showed off Redwood, an AI inference accelerator for robots and drones, in August. In that case, the company says its AI generated the RTL, verification, firmware, drivers, and kernels in under two weeks from a spec written by two human architects. Redwood still runs only on an FPGA and hasn’t been made in silicon, though the company says it is working toward having it built at TSMC. What to read next ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC OpenAI's AI models boost AMD's upcoming flagship GPU design by up to 14% in PPA AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’ Tendrils Compute, a possible rival based in Cambridge, U.K., raised funding earlier this month for a processor it says will have “thousands of cores operating in parallel.” It is also developing Vine, the same language Frostbite’s programs are written in.Architect Labs says more benchmarks are coming, but they’re only part of the plan. It also wants an FPGA-hosted “software playground for anybody to run a program on Frostbite” along with a “preliminary operating system.” Eventually, it plans to release Frostbite’s RTL and instruction set.In the meantime, the company plans to cover more workloads and compare “a broader set of CPUs,” including larger Frostbite mesh configurations against multicore versions of the comparison core with large caches. It also plans to test against “larger, wider, out-of-order CPUs,” with these comparisons due in the coming months on popular CPU benchmark suites such as SPEC and PARSEC. items.titleZh: 初创公司称，AI智能体从零开始设计出全新的CPU架构
items.descriptionZh:
Architect Labs是一家位于帕洛阿尔托的初创公司。该公司在研究博客中称，其AI系统从零开始发现、设计并验证了一款通用CPU——Frostbite，并为它设计了全新的指令集。Frostbite并非传统CPU的增量改进，而是围绕一种不同的计算范式构建。根据其公布的模拟结果，在25项工作负载中，由四个tile组成的Frostbite集群，其每瓦性能达到一个尺寸相近、已经过硅验证的双发射顺序执行CPU核心的4.59倍。不过，这些数据来自尚未流片的模拟7nm设计，并非实测芯片；公司还表示，出于法律原因，不能公开作为对比的传统CPU核心名称。

传统CPU依赖硬件在运行时“重新发现”哪些指令彼此存在依赖关系，并通过乱序执行等机制挖掘指令级并行。多核设计则通常需要较深的缓存层级和缓存一致性协议，以保证每个核心看到的共享内存视图一致，但这些机制扩展性有限，还会增加芯片面积和功耗。Architect Labs提出的替代思路是所谓的“免费多线程”：由程序本身直接暴露可并行的工作，而不需要线程、锁，也不需要为发现并行性而加入复杂的乱序硬件。

Frostbite的核心技术基础是“交互网”（interaction nets）。这是一种可追溯到1990年的计算模型：程序被表示为由节点构成的图，计算通过重写相连的节点对来完成。芯片设计围绕这一范式展开。由于被重写的节点对不会重叠，它们可以按任意顺序执行，也可以同时执行，最终得到相同结果。与此同时，每个值都恰好使用一次，因此数据可以留在较小的本地内存中，而不必依赖大型共享缓存。这也意味着Frostbite不需要传统多核CPU那种复杂的缓存一致性和深层缓存体系。

团队给出的例子是一个5×5棋盘上放置五个皇后、且彼此不能攻击的搜索问题。典型程序通常逐棋盘搜索解；而将同一问题表示为交互网后，搜索被拆分为3183个小操作，其中必须顺序执行的最长依赖链只有262步，因此在每一步平均约有12个操作已经准备好并行执行。关键在于，程序本身没有被改写，这种并行性已经内在存在于问题之中。

在硬件结构上，Frostbite由多个相同的tile组成，每个tile是一个小型处理单元，并通过片上网络连接，各自配有小型本地内存。此次用于性能对比的是四tile集群，外加四个L3节点；完整设计的布局则包含16个tile。该设计在早期综合阶段达到800MHz，但在最终布局中为500MHz。除每瓦性能外，该四tile集群的平均每面积性能达到对比核心的8.77倍。

其每瓦性能提升随工作负载不同而变化：25项工作负载的几何平均为4.59倍；用于调优设计的10项工作负载为6.02倍；留到最终评估的15项工作负载为3.83倍。表现最好的是留出工作负载conv2d，达到23.12倍；表现最差的是同样留出的递归Fibonacci，仅为1.15倍。这说明Frostbite的优势高度依赖工作负载中天然存在的并行结构，并非对所有程序都能带来同等幅度提升。

值得注意的是，构建Frostbite的AI系统最初从公司所称的“零架构先验”开始，不过团队首先选定了必须表现良好的工作负载。这种从空白出发的方式可能有助于避免人类先验带来的偏见。AI代理阅读论文和基准测试，构建Python模型，然后选择一个概念重点推进。最初生成的141页PDF包含编程模型、运行时和高级模块，但在首个寄存器传输级（RTL）设计生成后即被删除，因为其中许多数字和估计与物理可行性相差甚远。该PDF只是起点。选定架构后，代理们不再用英语写规范，因为英语无法保证每个细节正确或捕捉每个错误，而是改用公司自有的ASL语言。ASL可转换为Lean证明检查器，因此规范可以被机器检查。公司称，这能阻止一大类bug，并减少AI代理为达成目标而“钻空子”的行为。随后，代理们用ASL构建了Arcmodel，这是整个芯片的软件模型，早于任何电路设计存在。

由于RTL仿真速度慢，代理们转而在Arcmodel上测试想法，速度快约200倍。最初模型的功耗估计偏差最高接近250%，但一个自动化循环不断调整模型，最终使其与电路设计之间的偏差控制在5%以内。此后，多个代理并行提出修改建议，每个建议都要对照规范检查、在快速模型中试验、纳入电路设计并测量功耗，然后决定保留或放弃。最终共有58个想法被尝试，37个被保留。此外，还涌现出一种“从未由任何人类指定”的行为，即work stealing：没有工作的tile可以从邻居处拉取空闲工作；如果实在没有任务，也可以进入空闲状态以节省功耗。

从能量分布看，在一个四tile集群、20项工作负载平均值、排除时钟分配的口径下，对比核心与Frostbite的能耗结构差异明显：内存分别占57%和38%；取指、解码和发射指令分别占27%和6%；片上网络与调度器在对比核心中未单独列出，在Frostbite中占26%。若把时钟分配计入总能量，对比核心为49%，Frostbite为41%。这反映出Frostbite将更多能量用于片上网络和调度，同时大幅降低了传统指令取指、解码和发射以及内存体系上的开销。

Frostbite并非Architect Labs的第一款AI辅助设计芯片。该公司曾在8月展示Redwood，这是一款面向机器人和无人机的AI推理加速器。公司称，AI根据两名人类架构师编写的规范，在不到两周内生成了RTL、验证、固件、驱动和内核。Redwood目前仍只运行在FPGA上，尚未流片，但公司表示正推动在台积电制造。另一家位于英国剑桥的潜在竞争对手Tendrils Compute本月早些时候融资，声称将推出“数千核心并行运行”的处理器，并且也在开发Vine语言——Frostbite程序所使用的同一种语言。

Architect Labs表示，更多基准测试即将公布，但这只是计划的一部分。公司还希望推出一个由FPGA托管的“软件游乐场”，让任何人都能在Frostbite上运行程序，并提供“初步操作系统”。最终，公司计划发布Frostbite的RTL和指令集。在此之前，公司计划覆盖更多工作负载，并比较“更广泛的CPU”，包括更大规模的Frostbite mesh配置，与带大缓存的多核版对比核心进行比较；还计划测试更大、更宽、乱序执行的CPU。这些比较预计将在未来几个月内使用SPEC、PARSEC等流行CPU基准套件展开。总体来看，Frostbite展示了一种由AI参与从架构探索到规范验证、RTL生成和功耗优化的芯片设计路径，也提出了一种以交互网和显式并行替代传统乱序执行与深层缓存一致性的通用CPU方向；但其性能优势目前仍建立在模拟和特定工作负载之上，距离流片验证和广泛生态落地还有明显距离。

items.title: Moore Threads' next 'Lushan' gaming GPU could pack a record 64GB of VRAM
items.description: Moore Threads teased its Lushan gaming GPU ahead of MDC 2026, with a product manager claiming record VRAM for a consumer graphics card.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Moore Threads’ MTT S80 product manager says that the next Lushan gaming GPU will have more VRAM than any consumer graphics card currently available, VideoCardz reports. With Nvidia’s RTX 5090 already at 32GB, Lushan would need more than that. This matches the previous promise of four times the company’s MTT S80’s 16GB, putting the flagship Lushan at 64GB.Moore Threads apparently hasn’t given up on graphics, even four years after the MTT S80’s release. The company teased the card earlier this week with a poster for MDC 2026, its developer conference, showing a graphics card under a black cloth on a mountainside, and put Lushan’s name in the title of the post. It has previously indicated that Lushan products would arrive before the end of the year.Although nothing the product manager stated is an official statement, his words suggest that the new Lushan GPU could feature the largest memory capacity yet offered on a consumer graphics card, which certainly draws a lot of attention from gamers and local AI enthusiasts alike. As it stands, the 32GB RTX 5090 was available at $6,599 in our recent Newegg check, more than three times its MSRP, which illustrates the astronomical demand.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Swipe to scroll horizontally Graphics card memory comparison Card Class Memory Price Moore Threads Lushan Consumer (upcoming) Not disclosed; “4x” the S80 claimed, up to 64GB by our math Not announced Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 Consumer 32GB GDDR7 $1,999 MSRP; from $6,599 at Newegg (Nov. 15) Moore Threads MTT S80 Consumer 16GB GDDR6 2,999 yuan with a motherboard (about $410) at launch; 1,499 yuan (about $225) at JD.com, Nov. 21 Lisuan 7G106 / 7G105 Consumer / enterprise 12GB / 24GB — Intel Arc Pro B60 Dual (Maxsun) Workstation, two GPUs 2x 24GB GDDR6 — Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Workstation 96GB GDDR7 — Modded RTX 5090 (China) Gray market 96GB (as listed) $3,888 listing (Image credit: Moore Threads)The Lushan would be a graphics rendering chip based on the Huagang architecture, with a sibling Huashan for AI. Performance claims are lofty at 15x for AAA gaming, 50x ray tracing, 64x AI compute, and 16x geometry processing over the MTT S80, based on information from MDC 2025, last year’s edition of the conference. To get there, Lushan adds a new hardware ray-tracing engine, the UniTE rendering architecture, AI generative rendering, which MyDrivers describes as the manufacturer’s answer to Nvidia’s DLSS and AMD’s FSR for upscaling and multi-frame generation, and DirectX 12 Ultimate support.This is a mighty high goal, as the previous outing, with the S80, fell short of expectations. Released in November 2022 at 2,999 yuan (about $410), the S80 was at first sold only in a bundle with an Asus motherboard. It now costs about half that in China, despite rising GPU costs. The 16GB GDDR6, PCIe 5.0 GPU, which pulls 255W, only matched a low-end card when tested on immature drivers in early 2023; it struggled against a GT 1030.Moore Threads said last December that it had shipped monthly driver updates since and claimed the S80 then benchmarked 3.4x higher than at launch. The new 15x target is more reasonable when put against the backdrop of just how far the S80 trailed when it landed. You may like China-modified Nvidia RTX 5090 with massive 96GB of memory appears on Alibaba for less than $4,000 Gaming takes a backseat as Nvidia overhauls the RTX 5090 for maximum AI margins Nvidia's unreleased RTX 3070 Ti 16GB gets rebuilt by Brazilian modder using GDDR6 chips If we look beyond the consumer space, there are plenty of cards that have more than 32GB, and 64GB for that matter. The Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell workstation card, for instance, has 96GB of GDDR7. It’s also possible to get RTX 4090s rebuilt with 48GB, at least in some Chinese shops, and a listing in September offered an RTX 5090 modded to 96GB. Maxsun also has the Arc Pro B60 Dual, built on Intel GPUs, with 2x 24GB on just one board. However, memory supply remains tight, with crushing memory shortages, and is projected to remain so, while GDDR7 remains quite costly.Domestic rival Lisuan’s G100, meanwhile, is only at 12GB and 24GB for consumer and enterprise. A 64GB Lushan would leave those in the dust, which may hint that Moore Threads is targeting Western cards rather than just domestic rivals. It also raises the question of just how much memory you need for certain workloads.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsFurther revelation may come at MDC 2026, Dec. 29–30, at Zhongguancun International Innovation Center in Beijing, during a keynote by CEO Zhang Jianzhong. The keynote starts at 9:30 a.m. Beijing time on Dec. 29 (8:30 p.m. ET on Dec. 28), and Moore Threads says it will bring new flagship products, technologies, and solutions. items.titleZh: 摩尔线程下一代“庐山”游戏GPU或将配备创纪录的64GB显存
items.descriptionZh:
摩尔线程正筹备新一代“庐山”（Lushan）游戏GPU。据VideoCardz报道，MTT S80产品经理表示，庐山将配备超过当前任何消费级显卡的显存容量。目前Nvidia RTX 5090的显存为32GB，因此庐山至少要超过32GB；若与此前“达到MTT S80的16GB四倍”的说法一致，旗舰庐山可能达到64GB。不过，产品经理的表态并非官方声明，最终规格仍需以发布信息为准。摩尔线程在本周MDC 2026开发者大会的海报中预热了这款产品：黑色幕布覆盖山坡上的一台显卡，帖子标题出现“Lushan”。公司此前曾表示庐山产品将在年底前推出。若64GB成真，它将成为消费级显卡中最大的显存配置之一，也会吸引游戏玩家和本地AI爱好者关注。

从架构看，庐山将是一款基于Huagang架构的图形渲染芯片，另有面向AI的兄弟产品Huashan。摩尔线程在MDC 2025上给出的目标相当激进：相较MTT S80，庐山在AAA游戏性能上提升15倍、光线追踪提升50倍、AI算力提升64倍、几何处理提升16倍。为实现这些目标，庐山将新增硬件光线追踪引擎、UniTE渲染架构、AI生成式渲染，以及DirectX 12 Ultimate支持。其中，AI生成式渲染被MyDrivers描述为摩尔线程对标Nvidia DLSS和AMD FSR的方案，用于上采样和多帧生成。这些目标很高，因为上一代S80的实际表现未达预期。S80于2022年11月发布，首发价2999元（约410美元），最初只与华硕主板捆绑销售；其规格为16GB GDDR6、PCIe 5.0、255W功耗。2023年初在不够成熟的驱动下测试时，它仅相当于低端显卡，甚至难以对抗GT 1030。摩尔线程去年12月表示，自那以后每月发布驱动更新，并称S80当时的基准测试成绩较发布时提升3.4倍。考虑到S80落地时的性能基数较低，庐山相对S80提升15倍的目标显得更合理，但仍是艰巨挑战。

显存对比方面，RTX 5090为32GB GDDR7，官方建议零售价1999美元；Tom’s Hardware在11月15日查看Newegg时，其售价从6599美元起，超过建议零售价三倍，显示市场需求极高。MTT S80为16GB GDDR6，首发2999元含主板（约410美元），11月21日京东价格约1499元（约225美元）。国内竞争对手砺算的7G106/7G105面向消费和企业市场，显存分别为12GB和24GB。若庐山达到64GB，将明显拉开与国内竞品的差距，可能意味着摩尔线程不仅瞄准国内对手，也试图对标西方显卡。不过，64GB也引发“某些工作负载究竟需要多少显存”的讨论。放眼消费级之外，已有大量超过32GB甚至64GB的产品：Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell工作站卡配备96GB GDDR7；Maxsun的Intel Arc Pro B60 Dual单板集成两个GPU，共2×24GB GDDR6；中国部分店铺可提供48GB改装的RTX 4090，9月还有 listings 显示96GB改装的RTX 5090，标价3888美元。但当前显存供应紧张、短缺严重且预计持续，GDDR7成本仍然很高。

技术影响和应用场景上，大显存在高分辨率游戏、光线追踪、多帧生成、本地AI推理和大模型运行中具有吸引力，尤其适合需要在消费级硬件上承载更大模型或更高分辨率纹理的用户。但显存容量并非性能的全部，实际游戏和AI表现仍取决于GPU架构、显存带宽、驱动成熟度、软件生态和合作伙伴支持。摩尔线程计划在MDC 2026进一步披露信息。大会将于12月29日至30日在北京中关村国际创新中心举行，CEO张建中将在北京时间12月29日上午9:30（美东时间12月28日晚8:30）发表主题演讲，摩尔线程称将带来新的旗舰产品、技术和解决方案。庐山的最终规格、价格和上市时间预计届时或后续官方信息中揭晓。

items.title: Lenders back SpaceX's $43 billion Nvidia GPU deal but worry the collateral could end up in orbit, making them impossible to reclaim if Musk defaults
items.description: The $43 billion loan is structured as a unique arrangement in which a different company buys the Nvidia chips, while SpaceX makes quarterly payments to use them.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk is borrowing $43 billion to finance SpaceX's acquisition of Nvidia AI chips for its ambitious data center projects and is using the semiconductors as collateral. However, Ars Technica reports that lenders are concerned that SpaceX will use the chips for its planned orbital data center, making it difficult, if not impossible, for creditors to reclaim in case the company defaults on its loan. SpaceX said it will deploy the collateralized chips only on Earth, but it remains unclear whether this provision is included in the signed debt instrument.SpaceX is working on building massive data centers on both Earth and in space. Musk has already revealed the company’s first-generation AI1 satellite, with a 120-kilowatt payload and a span that’s larger than a Boeing 747, while he’s also planning to build a $24-billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Starbase, Texas. These projects are in addition to the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 sites near the Tennessee-Mississippi border.Despite being one of the richest people on Earth right now, Musk is relying on a financing deal to acquire the chips he needs to achieve his dream of building an AI LLM that will “assist in the pursuit of understanding.” The $43 billion “Project Saturn” loan is also not structured like a typical loan, so its investment-grade rating would remain unaffected. Instead, it’s built similarly to aircraft leasing agreements, in which a leasing company buys the jets and leases them to the airline that wants to use them. This saves the airline from having to put up a significant amount of cash to get the airplanes that it needs.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: For this deal, the Saturn Funding Trust, a fully owned subsidiary of asset-backed lending company WHCO, would acquire the Nvidia GPUs for SpaceX, with the latter paying the former quarterly for the privilege of using the AI chips. The deal is also described as a “five-year triple-net, hell-or-high-water finance lease arrangement,” meaning SpaceX must pay the lease for five years, whether the chips break, become obsolete, or the project becomes unprofitable. It’s also responsible for all the expenses of operating the chips.These terms are very lender-friendly, as SpaceX basically assumes all the risks while also keeping them off its books. Rating agency Moody’s also said in its report that the chips will be deployed in SpaceX’s U.S. data centers. Nevertheless, the company’s plan to blast data centers into space is making some lenders nervous, regardless of its Earth-bound plans and promises. items.author: Jowi Morales
items.titleZh: 贷款方支持SpaceX的430亿美元英伟达GPU交易，但担心抵押品可能被送入轨道，若马斯克违约将无法收回
items.descriptionZh:
Elon Musk正通过一笔43亿美元贷款为SpaceX收购Nvidia AI芯片提供融资，用于其雄心勃勃的数据中心项目，并将这些半导体作为抵押品。Ars Technica报道称，贷方担心SpaceX会把芯片用于计划中的轨道数据中心，一旦公司违约，债权人将很难、甚至无法收回这些抵押资产。SpaceX表示，作为抵押的芯片只会部署在地球上，但目前尚不清楚这一限制是否被写入已签署的债务工具。这一争议的背景是，SpaceX正同时推进地球和太空中的大型数据中心建设。Musk已公布公司第一代AI1卫星，其有效载荷为120千瓦，跨度大于波音747；他还计划在得克萨斯州Starbase建设一座耗资240亿美元的燃气动力AI超级计算机。这些项目还包括田纳西州与密西西比州边界附近的Colossus 1和Colossus 2站点。尽管Musk是当前全球最富有的人之一，他仍依赖融资交易获取所需芯片，以实现构建一个“协助追求理解”的AI大语言模型的梦想。

这笔名为“Project Saturn”的43亿美元贷款结构并不同于典型贷款，因此其投资级评级不会受到影响。相反，它类似飞机租赁协议：租赁公司购买飞机，再租给需要使用飞机的航空公司，从而使航空公司无需一次性投入大量现金。具体到该交易，资产支持贷款公司WHCO的全资子公司Saturn Funding Trust将为SpaceX购买Nvidia GPU，SpaceX则按季度向该信托支付使用AI芯片的费用。该交易被描述为“五年期三重净额、无论如何都要付（hell-or-high-water）的融资租赁安排”，意味着无论芯片损坏、过时，还是项目变得不盈利，SpaceX都必须支付五年租赁费；同时，SpaceX还负责芯片运营的全部费用。这些条款对贷方非常友好，因为SpaceX基本上承担了所有风险，同时又将相关负债保持在资产负债表之外。评级机构穆迪也在报告中表示，这些芯片将部署在SpaceX的美国数据中心。尽管如此，该公司将数据中心送入太空的计划仍让部分贷方感到紧张，即便SpaceX已就地球部署计划和承诺作出保证。

从技术原理看，这一安排的核心是把高价值AI芯片作为可融资资产，通过信托持有所有权、SpaceX支付租赁费的方式，实现类似飞机租赁的表外融资。其创新点在于将GPU等快速迭代的半导体纳入“三重净额”融资租赁结构：承租人承担维护、保险、税费等全部运营成本，并承担芯片损坏、过时和项目不盈利的风险，从而让贷方获得较强保护。但芯片作为抵押品存在特殊性：折旧快、技术更新快，且物理位置直接影响资产回收。若芯片被部署到轨道数据中心，债权人在地面法律框架下收回资产的难度将显著上升。性能参数方面，AI1卫星的120千瓦载荷和大于波音747的跨度显示出太空算力平台的大型化趋势；地面项目则包括240亿美元的Starbase燃气动力AI超级计算机，以及Colossus 1和Colossus 2站点。应用场景主要是为大语言模型训练和推理提供大规模算力，并支撑SpaceX在地球与太空构建分布式AI基础设施的长期目标。该融资结构在降低短期现金压力的同时，也把技术过时、资产位置和违约回收等风险集中暴露给融资各方，成为贷方担忧的焦点。

history.title: AI agents design an entirely new CPU architecture from scratch, startup claims
history.description: Architect Labs says its AI agents designed Frostbite, an interaction-net CPU with 4.59x the performance per watt of an in-order core.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Architect Labs, a Palo Alto startup, said in a research blog post that its AI systems discovered, designed, and verified Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set “built from the ground up.” Across 25 workloads, a four-tile Frostbite cluster delivered 4.59 times the performance per watt of a similarly sized “silicon-proven” dual-issue, in-order CPU core. Those numbers come from a simulated 7nm design that has not yet been made in silicon, and the company says it can’t name the comparison core for legal reasons.Conventional CPUs have hardware that “rediscovers, at runtime, which instructions actually depend on each other.” Multicore designs also need deep cache hierarchies and coherence protocols, which keep every core’s view of shared memory consistent, but scale poorly and cost area and power. Architect Labs’ alternative is what it calls “multithreading for free,” where the program itself exposes the parallel work, without threads, locks, or out-of-order hardware required for that discovery.Frostbite’s programs are compiled to interaction nets, a model of computation from 1990 in which a program is a graph of nodes and computation happens by rewriting pairs of connected nodes, and the chip is designed around this distinct paradigm. Pairs of nodes being rewritten never overlap, so they can run in any order, or all at once, and arrive at the same result. Every value is also used exactly once, so data can stay in small local memories instead of large shared caches.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: An example of the difference given by the team is a 5x5 chess-like board with five queens, placed so none can attack another. A typical program searches for solutions one board at a time. As an interaction net, the same search breaks into 3,183 small operations, and the longest chain that has to run in order is only 262 steps, so on average about 12 operations are ready to run at once at each step. Nothing about the program was rewritten to get there, as the parallel work was already intrinsic. (Image credit: Architect Labs)Each of the chip’s tiles, small identical processing units linked by an on-chip network, has its own small local memory. Four tiles, plus four L3 nodes, form the cluster that’s benchmarked against the conventional core for the performance claims, but the full layout has 16 tiles. The design reached 800 MHz in early synthesis but ended up at 500 MHz in the final layout. The cluster also averaged 8.77 times the comparison core’s performance per area, and the table below shows how its performance per watt varies by workload. You may like Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests Nuvacore reveals unconventional Core First CPU IP design strategy Bizarre AI chip demo uses butter to highlight how new chip runs 40 degrees cooler than the competition Swipe to scroll horizontally How Frostbite’s efficiency gains vary by workload Workloads Frostbite performance per watt vs. comparison core All 25 (geometric mean) 4.59x 10 used to tune the design 6.02x 15 held out until the final evaluation 3.83x Best: conv2d (held out) 23.12x Worst: recursive Fibonacci (held out) 1.15x It may come as some surprise that the AI which built Frostbite started with what the company calls “zero architectural priors,” though the team first picked the workloads it had to do well on, and this sort of blank slatism may have its advantages in avoiding bias. Instead, the agents read papers and benchmarks, built Python models, and then selected one concept for focus. The original 141-page PDF output, which contained a programming model, runtime, and high-level blocks, was deleted after the first register-transfer level (RTL) design was generated, because “many of the numbers and estimates were well off what was physically possible.”That PDF was only ever a starting point. Once the agents picked an architecture, they moved away from English — as it can’t get every detail right or catch every mistake, according to the team — and wrote the spec in the company’s own language, called ASL. ASL translates to Lean, a proof checker, so it can be machine-checked, which the company says stops a large class of bugs and cuts down on agents gaming their objectives. From this, the agents devised Arcmodel, a software model of the whole chip written in ASL, before any circuit design existed.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsSimulating the RTL is slow, so the agents tested ideas on the model instead, which ran about 200 times faster. At first, the model’s power estimates were off by up to almost 250%, but an automated loop adjusted it until it matched the circuit design within just 5%.From there, swarms of agents proposed changes in parallel, and each one was checked against the spec, tried in the fast model, built into the circuit design, and measured for power before being kept or dropped. This led to 58 ideas tried, with 37 kept. Separately, a behavior emerged that “was never specified by any human,” in what is known as work stealing: a tile with nothing to do can pull spare work from a neighbor or, in lieu of anything to do, go idle to save power. Swipe to scroll horizontally Where each chip’s energy goes Share of energy (one four-tile cluster, mean of 20 workloads, excluding clock distribution) Comparison core Frostbite Memory 57% 38% Fetching, decoding, and issuing instructions 27% 6% On-chip network and scheduler Not broken out 26% Clock distribution (share of total energy, left out of the rows above) 49% 41% This isn’t Architect Labs’ first design, as it showed off Redwood, an AI inference accelerator for robots and drones, in August. In that case, the company says its AI generated the RTL, verification, firmware, drivers, and kernels in under two weeks from a spec written by two human architects. Redwood still runs only on an FPGA and hasn’t been made in silicon, though the company says it is working toward having it built at TSMC. What to read next ‘This is how AI should be used’ — OpenAI head of hardware breaks down the AI-assisted design of its Jalapeño ASIC OpenAI's AI models boost AMD's upcoming flagship GPU design by up to 14% in PPA AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’ Tendrils Compute, a possible rival based in Cambridge, U.K., raised funding earlier this month for a processor it says will have “thousands of cores operating in parallel.” It is also developing Vine, the same language Frostbite’s programs are written in.Architect Labs says more benchmarks are coming, but they’re only part of the plan. It also wants an FPGA-hosted “software playground for anybody to run a program on Frostbite” along with a “preliminary operating system.” Eventually, it plans to release Frostbite’s RTL and instruction set.In the meantime, the company plans to cover more workloads and compare “a broader set of CPUs,” including larger Frostbite mesh configurations against multicore versions of the comparison core with large caches. It also plans to test against “larger, wider, out-of-order CPUs,” with these comparisons due in the coming months on popular CPU benchmark suites such as SPEC and PARSEC. history.author: Shane Downing
history.titleZh: 初创公司称，AI智能体从零开始设计出全新的CPU架构
history.descriptionZh:
Architect Labs是一家位于帕洛阿尔托的初创公司。该公司在研究博客中称，其AI系统从零开始发现、设计并验证了一款通用CPU——Frostbite，并为它设计了全新的指令集。Frostbite并非传统CPU的增量改进，而是围绕一种不同的计算范式构建。根据其公布的模拟结果，在25项工作负载中，由四个tile组成的Frostbite集群，其每瓦性能达到一个尺寸相近、已经过硅验证的双发射顺序执行CPU核心的4.59倍。不过，这些数据来自尚未流片的模拟7nm设计，并非实测芯片；公司还表示，出于法律原因，不能公开作为对比的传统CPU核心名称。

传统CPU依赖硬件在运行时“重新发现”哪些指令彼此存在依赖关系，并通过乱序执行等机制挖掘指令级并行。多核设计则通常需要较深的缓存层级和缓存一致性协议，以保证每个核心看到的共享内存视图一致，但这些机制扩展性有限，还会增加芯片面积和功耗。Architect Labs提出的替代思路是所谓的“免费多线程”：由程序本身直接暴露可并行的工作，而不需要线程、锁，也不需要为发现并行性而加入复杂的乱序硬件。

Frostbite的核心技术基础是“交互网”（interaction nets）。这是一种可追溯到1990年的计算模型：程序被表示为由节点构成的图，计算通过重写相连的节点对来完成。芯片设计围绕这一范式展开。由于被重写的节点对不会重叠，它们可以按任意顺序执行，也可以同时执行，最终得到相同结果。与此同时，每个值都恰好使用一次，因此数据可以留在较小的本地内存中，而不必依赖大型共享缓存。这也意味着Frostbite不需要传统多核CPU那种复杂的缓存一致性和深层缓存体系。

团队给出的例子是一个5×5棋盘上放置五个皇后、且彼此不能攻击的搜索问题。典型程序通常逐棋盘搜索解；而将同一问题表示为交互网后，搜索被拆分为3183个小操作，其中必须顺序执行的最长依赖链只有262步，因此在每一步平均约有12个操作已经准备好并行执行。关键在于，程序本身没有被改写，这种并行性已经内在存在于问题之中。

在硬件结构上，Frostbite由多个相同的tile组成，每个tile是一个小型处理单元，并通过片上网络连接，各自配有小型本地内存。此次用于性能对比的是四tile集群，外加四个L3节点；完整设计的布局则包含16个tile。该设计在早期综合阶段达到800MHz，但在最终布局中为500MHz。除每瓦性能外，该四tile集群的平均每面积性能达到对比核心的8.77倍。

其每瓦性能提升随工作负载不同而变化：25项工作负载的几何平均为4.59倍；用于调优设计的10项工作负载为6.02倍；留到最终评估的15项工作负载为3.83倍。表现最好的是留出工作负载conv2d，达到23.12倍；表现最差的是同样留出的递归Fibonacci，仅为1.15倍。这说明Frostbite的优势高度依赖工作负载中天然存在的并行结构，并非对所有程序都能带来同等幅度提升。

值得注意的是，构建Frostbite的AI系统最初从公司所称的“零架构先验”开始，不过团队首先选定了必须表现良好的工作负载。这种从空白出发的方式可能有助于避免人类先验带来的偏见。AI代理阅读论文和基准测试，构建Python模型，然后选择一个概念重点推进。最初生成的141页PDF包含编程模型、运行时和高级模块，但在首个寄存器传输级（RTL）设计生成后即被删除，因为其中许多数字和估计与物理可行性相差甚远。该PDF只是起点。选定架构后，代理们不再用英语写规范，因为英语无法保证每个细节正确或捕捉每个错误，而是改用公司自有的ASL语言。ASL可转换为Lean证明检查器，因此规范可以被机器检查。公司称，这能阻止一大类bug，并减少AI代理为达成目标而“钻空子”的行为。随后，代理们用ASL构建了Arcmodel，这是整个芯片的软件模型，早于任何电路设计存在。

由于RTL仿真速度慢，代理们转而在Arcmodel上测试想法，速度快约200倍。最初模型的功耗估计偏差最高接近250%，但一个自动化循环不断调整模型，最终使其与电路设计之间的偏差控制在5%以内。此后，多个代理并行提出修改建议，每个建议都要对照规范检查、在快速模型中试验、纳入电路设计并测量功耗，然后决定保留或放弃。最终共有58个想法被尝试，37个被保留。此外，还涌现出一种“从未由任何人类指定”的行为，即work stealing：没有工作的tile可以从邻居处拉取空闲工作；如果实在没有任务，也可以进入空闲状态以节省功耗。

从能量分布看，在一个四tile集群、20项工作负载平均值、排除时钟分配的口径下，对比核心与Frostbite的能耗结构差异明显：内存分别占57%和38%；取指、解码和发射指令分别占27%和6%；片上网络与调度器在对比核心中未单独列出，在Frostbite中占26%。若把时钟分配计入总能量，对比核心为49%，Frostbite为41%。这反映出Frostbite将更多能量用于片上网络和调度，同时大幅降低了传统指令取指、解码和发射以及内存体系上的开销。

Frostbite并非Architect Labs的第一款AI辅助设计芯片。该公司曾在8月展示Redwood，这是一款面向机器人和无人机的AI推理加速器。公司称，AI根据两名人类架构师编写的规范，在不到两周内生成了RTL、验证、固件、驱动和内核。Redwood目前仍只运行在FPGA上，尚未流片，但公司表示正推动在台积电制造。另一家位于英国剑桥的潜在竞争对手Tendrils Compute本月早些时候融资，声称将推出“数千核心并行运行”的处理器，并且也在开发Vine语言——Frostbite程序所使用的同一种语言。

Architect Labs表示，更多基准测试即将公布，但这只是计划的一部分。公司还希望推出一个由FPGA托管的“软件游乐场”，让任何人都能在Frostbite上运行程序，并提供“初步操作系统”。最终，公司计划发布Frostbite的RTL和指令集。在此之前，公司计划覆盖更多工作负载，并比较“更广泛的CPU”，包括更大规模的Frostbite mesh配置，与带大缓存的多核版对比核心进行比较；还计划测试更大、更宽、乱序执行的CPU。这些比较预计将在未来几个月内使用SPEC、PARSEC等流行CPU基准套件展开。总体来看，Frostbite展示了一种由AI参与从架构探索到规范验证、RTL生成和功耗优化的芯片设计路径，也提出了一种以交互网和显式并行替代传统乱序执行与深层缓存一致性的通用CPU方向；但其性能优势目前仍建立在模拟和特定工作负载之上，距离流片验证和广泛生态落地还有明显距离。

history.title: Moore Threads' next 'Lushan' gaming GPU could pack a record 64GB of VRAM
history.description: Moore Threads teased its Lushan gaming GPU ahead of MDC 2026, with a product manager claiming record VRAM for a consumer graphics card.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Moore Threads’ MTT S80 product manager says that the next Lushan gaming GPU will have more VRAM than any consumer graphics card currently available, VideoCardz reports. With Nvidia’s RTX 5090 already at 32GB, Lushan would need more than that. This matches the previous promise of four times the company’s MTT S80’s 16GB, putting the flagship Lushan at 64GB.Moore Threads apparently hasn’t given up on graphics, even four years after the MTT S80’s release. The company teased the card earlier this week with a poster for MDC 2026, its developer conference, showing a graphics card under a black cloth on a mountainside, and put Lushan’s name in the title of the post. It has previously indicated that Lushan products would arrive before the end of the year.Although nothing the product manager stated is an official statement, his words suggest that the new Lushan GPU could feature the largest memory capacity yet offered on a consumer graphics card, which certainly draws a lot of attention from gamers and local AI enthusiasts alike. As it stands, the 32GB RTX 5090 was available at $6,599 in our recent Newegg check, more than three times its MSRP, which illustrates the astronomical demand.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Swipe to scroll horizontally Graphics card memory comparison Card Class Memory Price Moore Threads Lushan Consumer (upcoming) Not disclosed; “4x” the S80 claimed, up to 64GB by our math Not announced Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 Consumer 32GB GDDR7 $1,999 MSRP; from $6,599 at Newegg (Nov. 15) Moore Threads MTT S80 Consumer 16GB GDDR6 2,999 yuan with a motherboard (about $410) at launch; 1,499 yuan (about $225) at JD.com, Nov. 21 Lisuan 7G106 / 7G105 Consumer / enterprise 12GB / 24GB — Intel Arc Pro B60 Dual (Maxsun) Workstation, two GPUs 2x 24GB GDDR6 — Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Workstation 96GB GDDR7 — Modded RTX 5090 (China) Gray market 96GB (as listed) $3,888 listing (Image credit: Moore Threads)The Lushan would be a graphics rendering chip based on the Huagang architecture, with a sibling Huashan for AI. Performance claims are lofty at 15x for AAA gaming, 50x ray tracing, 64x AI compute, and 16x geometry processing over the MTT S80, based on information from MDC 2025, last year’s edition of the conference. To get there, Lushan adds a new hardware ray-tracing engine, the UniTE rendering architecture, AI generative rendering, which MyDrivers describes as the manufacturer’s answer to Nvidia’s DLSS and AMD’s FSR for upscaling and multi-frame generation, and DirectX 12 Ultimate support.This is a mighty high goal, as the previous outing, with the S80, fell short of expectations. Released in November 2022 at 2,999 yuan (about $410), the S80 was at first sold only in a bundle with an Asus motherboard. It now costs about half that in China, despite rising GPU costs. The 16GB GDDR6, PCIe 5.0 GPU, which pulls 255W, only matched a low-end card when tested on immature drivers in early 2023; it struggled against a GT 1030.Moore Threads said last December that it had shipped monthly driver updates since and claimed the S80 then benchmarked 3.4x higher than at launch. The new 15x target is more reasonable when put against the backdrop of just how far the S80 trailed when it landed. You may like China-modified Nvidia RTX 5090 with massive 96GB of memory appears on Alibaba for less than $4,000 Gaming takes a backseat as Nvidia overhauls the RTX 5090 for maximum AI margins Nvidia's unreleased RTX 3070 Ti 16GB gets rebuilt by Brazilian modder using GDDR6 chips If we look beyond the consumer space, there are plenty of cards that have more than 32GB, and 64GB for that matter. The Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell workstation card, for instance, has 96GB of GDDR7. It’s also possible to get RTX 4090s rebuilt with 48GB, at least in some Chinese shops, and a listing in September offered an RTX 5090 modded to 96GB. Maxsun also has the Arc Pro B60 Dual, built on Intel GPUs, with 2x 24GB on just one board. However, memory supply remains tight, with crushing memory shortages, and is projected to remain so, while GDDR7 remains quite costly.Domestic rival Lisuan’s G100, meanwhile, is only at 12GB and 24GB for consumer and enterprise. A 64GB Lushan would leave those in the dust, which may hint that Moore Threads is targeting Western cards rather than just domestic rivals. It also raises the question of just how much memory you need for certain workloads.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsFurther revelation may come at MDC 2026, Dec. 29–30, at Zhongguancun International Innovation Center in Beijing, during a keynote by CEO Zhang Jianzhong. The keynote starts at 9:30 a.m. Beijing time on Dec. 29 (8:30 p.m. ET on Dec. 28), and Moore Threads says it will bring new flagship products, technologies, and solutions. history.author: Shane Downing
history.titleZh: 摩尔线程下一代“庐山”游戏GPU或将配备创纪录的64GB显存
history.descriptionZh:
摩尔线程正筹备新一代“庐山”（Lushan）游戏GPU。据VideoCardz报道，MTT S80产品经理表示，庐山将配备超过当前任何消费级显卡的显存容量。目前Nvidia RTX 5090的显存为32GB，因此庐山至少要超过32GB；若与此前“达到MTT S80的16GB四倍”的说法一致，旗舰庐山可能达到64GB。不过，产品经理的表态并非官方声明，最终规格仍需以发布信息为准。摩尔线程在本周MDC 2026开发者大会的海报中预热了这款产品：黑色幕布覆盖山坡上的一台显卡，帖子标题出现“Lushan”。公司此前曾表示庐山产品将在年底前推出。若64GB成真，它将成为消费级显卡中最大的显存配置之一，也会吸引游戏玩家和本地AI爱好者关注。

从架构看，庐山将是一款基于Huagang架构的图形渲染芯片，另有面向AI的兄弟产品Huashan。摩尔线程在MDC 2025上给出的目标相当激进：相较MTT S80，庐山在AAA游戏性能上提升15倍、光线追踪提升50倍、AI算力提升64倍、几何处理提升16倍。为实现这些目标，庐山将新增硬件光线追踪引擎、UniTE渲染架构、AI生成式渲染，以及DirectX 12 Ultimate支持。其中，AI生成式渲染被MyDrivers描述为摩尔线程对标Nvidia DLSS和AMD FSR的方案，用于上采样和多帧生成。这些目标很高，因为上一代S80的实际表现未达预期。S80于2022年11月发布，首发价2999元（约410美元），最初只与华硕主板捆绑销售；其规格为16GB GDDR6、PCIe 5.0、255W功耗。2023年初在不够成熟的驱动下测试时，它仅相当于低端显卡，甚至难以对抗GT 1030。摩尔线程去年12月表示，自那以后每月发布驱动更新，并称S80当时的基准测试成绩较发布时提升3.4倍。考虑到S80落地时的性能基数较低，庐山相对S80提升15倍的目标显得更合理，但仍是艰巨挑战。

显存对比方面，RTX 5090为32GB GDDR7，官方建议零售价1999美元；Tom’s Hardware在11月15日查看Newegg时，其售价从6599美元起，超过建议零售价三倍，显示市场需求极高。MTT S80为16GB GDDR6，首发2999元含主板（约410美元），11月21日京东价格约1499元（约225美元）。国内竞争对手砺算的7G106/7G105面向消费和企业市场，显存分别为12GB和24GB。若庐山达到64GB，将明显拉开与国内竞品的差距，可能意味着摩尔线程不仅瞄准国内对手，也试图对标西方显卡。不过，64GB也引发“某些工作负载究竟需要多少显存”的讨论。放眼消费级之外，已有大量超过32GB甚至64GB的产品：Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell工作站卡配备96GB GDDR7；Maxsun的Intel Arc Pro B60 Dual单板集成两个GPU，共2×24GB GDDR6；中国部分店铺可提供48GB改装的RTX 4090，9月还有 listings 显示96GB改装的RTX 5090，标价3888美元。但当前显存供应紧张、短缺严重且预计持续，GDDR7成本仍然很高。

技术影响和应用场景上，大显存在高分辨率游戏、光线追踪、多帧生成、本地AI推理和大模型运行中具有吸引力，尤其适合需要在消费级硬件上承载更大模型或更高分辨率纹理的用户。但显存容量并非性能的全部，实际游戏和AI表现仍取决于GPU架构、显存带宽、驱动成熟度、软件生态和合作伙伴支持。摩尔线程计划在MDC 2026进一步披露信息。大会将于12月29日至30日在北京中关村国际创新中心举行，CEO张建中将在北京时间12月29日上午9:30（美东时间12月28日晚8:30）发表主题演讲，摩尔线程称将带来新的旗舰产品、技术和解决方案。庐山的最终规格、价格和上市时间预计届时或后续官方信息中揭晓。

history.title: Lenders back SpaceX's $43 billion Nvidia GPU deal but worry the collateral could end up in orbit, making them impossible to reclaim if Musk defaults
history.description: The $43 billion loan is structured as a unique arrangement in which a different company buys the Nvidia chips, while SpaceX makes quarterly payments to use them.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Instagram Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk is borrowing $43 billion to finance SpaceX's acquisition of Nvidia AI chips for its ambitious data center projects and is using the semiconductors as collateral. However, Ars Technica reports that lenders are concerned that SpaceX will use the chips for its planned orbital data center, making it difficult, if not impossible, for creditors to reclaim in case the company defaults on its loan. SpaceX said it will deploy the collateralized chips only on Earth, but it remains unclear whether this provision is included in the signed debt instrument.SpaceX is working on building massive data centers on both Earth and in space. Musk has already revealed the company’s first-generation AI1 satellite, with a 120-kilowatt payload and a span that’s larger than a Boeing 747, while he’s also planning to build a $24-billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Starbase, Texas. These projects are in addition to the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 sites near the Tennessee-Mississippi border.Despite being one of the richest people on Earth right now, Musk is relying on a financing deal to acquire the chips he needs to achieve his dream of building an AI LLM that will “assist in the pursuit of understanding.” The $43 billion “Project Saturn” loan is also not structured like a typical loan, so its investment-grade rating would remain unaffected. Instead, it’s built similarly to aircraft leasing agreements, in which a leasing company buys the jets and leases them to the airline that wants to use them. This saves the airline from having to put up a significant amount of cash to get the airplanes that it needs.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: For this deal, the Saturn Funding Trust, a fully owned subsidiary of asset-backed lending company WHCO, would acquire the Nvidia GPUs for SpaceX, with the latter paying the former quarterly for the privilege of using the AI chips. The deal is also described as a “five-year triple-net, hell-or-high-water finance lease arrangement,” meaning SpaceX must pay the lease for five years, whether the chips break, become obsolete, or the project becomes unprofitable. It’s also responsible for all the expenses of operating the chips.These terms are very lender-friendly, as SpaceX basically assumes all the risks while also keeping them off its books. Rating agency Moody’s also said in its report that the chips will be deployed in SpaceX’s U.S. data centers. Nevertheless, the company’s plan to blast data centers into space is making some lenders nervous, regardless of its Earth-bound plans and promises. history.titleZh: 贷款方支持SpaceX的430亿美元英伟达GPU交易，但担心抵押品可能被送入轨道，若马斯克违约将无法收回
history.descriptionZh:
Elon Musk正通过一笔43亿美元贷款为SpaceX收购Nvidia AI芯片提供融资，用于其雄心勃勃的数据中心项目，并将这些半导体作为抵押品。Ars Technica报道称，贷方担心SpaceX会把芯片用于计划中的轨道数据中心，一旦公司违约，债权人将很难、甚至无法收回这些抵押资产。SpaceX表示，作为抵押的芯片只会部署在地球上，但目前尚不清楚这一限制是否被写入已签署的债务工具。这一争议的背景是，SpaceX正同时推进地球和太空中的大型数据中心建设。Musk已公布公司第一代AI1卫星，其有效载荷为120千瓦，跨度大于波音747；他还计划在得克萨斯州Starbase建设一座耗资240亿美元的燃气动力AI超级计算机。这些项目还包括田纳西州与密西西比州边界附近的Colossus 1和Colossus 2站点。尽管Musk是当前全球最富有的人之一，他仍依赖融资交易获取所需芯片，以实现构建一个“协助追求理解”的AI大语言模型的梦想。

这笔名为“Project Saturn”的43亿美元贷款结构并不同于典型贷款，因此其投资级评级不会受到影响。相反，它类似飞机租赁协议：租赁公司购买飞机，再租给需要使用飞机的航空公司，从而使航空公司无需一次性投入大量现金。具体到该交易，资产支持贷款公司WHCO的全资子公司Saturn Funding Trust将为SpaceX购买Nvidia GPU，SpaceX则按季度向该信托支付使用AI芯片的费用。该交易被描述为“五年期三重净额、无论如何都要付（hell-or-high-water）的融资租赁安排”，意味着无论芯片损坏、过时，还是项目变得不盈利，SpaceX都必须支付五年租赁费；同时，SpaceX还负责芯片运营的全部费用。这些条款对贷方非常友好，因为SpaceX基本上承担了所有风险，同时又将相关负债保持在资产负债表之外。评级机构穆迪也在报告中表示，这些芯片将部署在SpaceX的美国数据中心。尽管如此，该公司将数据中心送入太空的计划仍让部分贷方感到紧张，即便SpaceX已就地球部署计划和承诺作出保证。

从技术原理看，这一安排的核心是把高价值AI芯片作为可融资资产，通过信托持有所有权、SpaceX支付租赁费的方式，实现类似飞机租赁的表外融资。其创新点在于将GPU等快速迭代的半导体纳入“三重净额”融资租赁结构：承租人承担维护、保险、税费等全部运营成本，并承担芯片损坏、过时和项目不盈利的风险，从而让贷方获得较强保护。但芯片作为抵押品存在特殊性：折旧快、技术更新快，且物理位置直接影响资产回收。若芯片被部署到轨道数据中心，债权人在地面法律框架下收回资产的难度将显著上升。性能参数方面，AI1卫星的120千瓦载荷和大于波音747的跨度显示出太空算力平台的大型化趋势；地面项目则包括240亿美元的Starbase燃气动力AI超级计算机，以及Colossus 1和Colossus 2站点。应用场景主要是为大语言模型训练和推理提供大规模算力，并支撑SpaceX在地球与太空构建分布式AI基础设施的长期目标。该融资结构在降低短期现金压力的同时，也把技术过时、资产位置和违约回收等风险集中暴露给融资各方，成为贷方担忧的焦点。
